pairs.difference: Both cards float the hero on tone-on-tone concentric rings (category 1) with no props. A's blue rings and B's orange rings have the same even band width and a soft bright centre. B's detail, 0.0071, sits just under the real range, but that gap is too small to read by eye.

A puts a grey flagstone floor with many crack lines under a candy-pink striped wall, which is an odd pairing, and adds a flame under the pot and bubbles drifting in the air above the rim. B has a wood plank ledge against a plain blue wall and no extras, though the wall's thin bright lines raise its edge count. The lean to A is weak and rests on the mismatched floor and added effects.
pairs.fix: Stand the pot on one plain, quiet stone surface with only two or three large slabs and no cracks. Keep the bubbles inside the rim, with nothing floating in the air.

pairs.difference: A floats on a soft blue spiral and B on soft blue waves. Both are tone-on-tone, both are in range, and neither has props. The spiral has more edges (0.016 against 0.004), but the anchor's wave and ray fields are equally plain, so this does not separate them.

B sets a pale pink-lilac sunburst over a wood deck that curves at the horizon and is scratched all over with cracks and split plank lines. Both background numbers are above the real range (0.0196 and 0.034). A's green ring field is quiet and in range, with nothing behind the envelope. The anchor's deck under the barrel has fewer, calmer plank lines.
pairs.fix: Draw the deck as a few wide, smooth planks with straight seams and no cracks or scratches. Use one calm background colour instead of the pale multi-colour sunburst.

pairs.difference: Both float on sunbursts with no props. In the lens, A's purple field keeps red-orange halos around all three flames, and the rays are low in detail (0.0067, below the real range). B's green and yellow rays are in range and have no halo on the field, only a broad central glow. The lean to A is slight.
pairs.fix: Keep the flame light on the candles only, with no coloured halo on the background. Use broad, plain rays.

pairs.difference: Both cards use a diamond tone-on-tone wall with a ledge, and both numbers are in range. B adds sparkle stars and tiny dots inside the ball, which is the invented sparkle this review looks for, and its ledge is a detailed wood shelf with a front edge. A's ledge is a plain flat purple band, closer to category 2 anchors.
pairs.fix: Remove the star sparkles and small dots, and leave only soft mist inside the glass.

pairs.difference: A has a striped wall and a floor of a few wide planks, the same quiet load as the anchor's barrel deck. B lays dozens of small bricks in rings around the fountain against the same striped wall, and its edge density, 0.046, is at the top of the real range. Curved ground shapes also appear on generated cards in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Replace the small brick ring with a plain floor of a few large, quiet shapes and fewer seams.

pairs.difference: B has only sky, clouds and a calm sea, and it matches the real lighthouse card from the lessons. A adds a large cratered moon in a bright daytime sky behind the chimney, tucks clouds in on both sides, and scatters grass tufts on the hill. The moon is an invented prop that competes with the roof, and it does not fit the daylight.
pairs.fix: Remove the moon. Use a plain blue sky with one or two soft clouds and a smooth hill without grass tufts.

pairs.difference: B matches the anchor's park staging: a large tree, round bushes and a winding path behind, with cast shadows on the lawn. A has a cartoon cratered moon in a daytime sky, two extra tombstones and grass tufts, with thin bushes behind. Its background numbers are at or below the bottom of the real range (0.0103 and 0.013). The moon and gravestones are story props, and the rest of the environment is sparse.
pairs.fix: Remove the moon and the tombstones. Set the object in a simple green park with one big tree, soft round bushes and a curving path, with shadows on the grass.

pairs.difference: Both use a warm wall and a pale ledge. A adds moss clumps and two fallen orange leaves on the plinth as small story decoration, and its background detail, 0.0058, is below the real range, with a hot yellow glow behind the stone. B has no added props, and its background is in range, with a plain orange wall and a clean horizon.
pairs.fix: Remove the moss and leaves. Stand the stone on a clean base with a flat, even backdrop and no glow behind it.

pairs.difference: B puts a curved sand mound under the rays, adds three pebbles nobody asked for around the base, and has a dark stain-like shadow on the sand at left that does not match the toy. A has only purple rays and straight wood planks, with no props, although the planks add edges (0.023). The curved ground matches generated cards in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Remove the pebbles and the stray dark patch. Make the ground a flat, plain band of sand with a straight horizon and one contact shadow.

pairs.difference: A has plain sky with soft clouds along the bottom and low numbers (0.0079 and 0.006), like the anchor's quiet skies. B stacks a foam collar, dark concentric ripple rings and clouds on both sides, and its edge density, 0.021, is above the real range. In the lighthouse lessons the generated sea is also busier than the real one. Here the ripple rings pull attention toward the buoy's base.
pairs.fix: Make the sea a calm band of blue with a few soft light streaks, with no ring ripples, and keep the clouds to one side.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away by adding things to the world around the hero. The clearest case is the cratered moon placed in a bright daytime sky on p08 A and p09 A. Other tells are small story props such as tombstones, grass tufts, moss, leaves and pebbles, and sparkle effects. Ground also runs too busy or wrong: cracked planks, many small bricks, ring ripples and curved mounds instead of a few large, quiet shapes with a straight horizon. Environments are also unbalanced, either over-scribbled or sparse where real cards use one big tree and a path. Abstract backdrops (rays, rings, spirals, stripes) mostly match the real cards, so on these fields staging gives little to separate them.
